summary:
S.J. Res. 183, introduced by Senator Booker in the 119th Congress (2d Session), is a privileged joint resolution invoking Congress's war powers to direct the withdrawal of United States Armed Forces from unauthorized hostilities within or against the Islamic Republic of Iran.

Section 1 sets forth fourteen findings establishing the resolution's constitutional and statutory predicate. These recite Congress's exclusive power to declare war under Article I, Section 8, Clause 11; the purpose and consultation requirements of the War Powers Resolution (sections 2(a) and 3, codified at 50 U.S.C. 1541(a) and 1542); and factual assertions that the President initiated "Operation Epic Fury" on February 28, 2026, conducting air and missile strikes inside Iran without congressional authorization or consultation. Finding (13) characterizes these operations as an "introduction of United States Armed Forces into hostilities" within the meaning of section 4(a) of the War Powers Resolution (50 U.S.C. 1543(a)). Finding (14) invokes section 1013 of the Department of State Authorization Act, Fiscal Years 1984 and 1985 (50 U.S.C. 1546a), which channels resolutions requiring removal of Armed Forces from hostilities into the expedited procedures of section 601(b) of the International Security Assistance and Arms Export Control Act of 1976 (Pub. L. 94-329).

Section 2(a) is the operative directive. Pursuant to 50 U.S.C. 1546a and in accordance with section 601(b) of Pub. L. 94-329, Congress directs the President to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities within or against Iran, unless such hostilities are "explicitly authorized by a declaration of war or a specific authorization for use of military force." The resolution invokes the expedited (privileged) procedural posture rather than relying on the automatic 60-day termination clock of the War Powers Resolution. The text specifies no removal deadline, appropriations, or amendments to existing law; it operates solely as a directive to the executive.

Section 2(b) contains a rule of construction preserving three categories of activity: (1) defending against attacks on the United States or its personnel or facilities abroad; (2) collecting, analyzing, or sharing intelligence—including with Israel and partner countries attacked by Iran since February 28, 2026, and other nations and international organizations—regarding threats from Iran or its proxies; and (3) assisting Israel and such partner countries in directly defending against retaliatory attacks by Iran or its proxies, or by providing defensive materiel support for such measures.

The resolution neither authorizes nor appropriates funds, and contains no severability clause, sunset provision, or specified effective date beyond enactment.
